name: Abbess Bugga
knownFor: An English abbess and friend of Boniface of Mainz. Her own letter of thanks to him survives. She governed a house of women, went to Rome to pray, and met Boniface there.
dates: Eighth century. Edward Kylie dates her letter to between 720 and 722, and the last letter about her to between 748 and 754. Bregwin of Canterbury gives her burial day as 27 December, with no year
place: England. Ethelbert the Second, king of Kent, calls her his kinswoman. No source used here names her monastery

keyWorks.title: Letter to Boniface
keyWorks.about: she gives thanks for his safe journey and his success, asks his prayers, and promises The Sufferings of the Martyrs. Kylie dates it to between 720 and 722 and gives it in English only

traces: With her mother, the abbess Eangyth, she wrote to Boniface of the souls in their care, their poverty and the hostility of the king.
Ethelbert the Second, king of Kent, writes that she governed a monastery of consecrated women "well under the law of the Church".
She sent Boniface fifty shillings, an altar pall, gifts and garments, and asked him for passages of Scripture.
remembered: Boniface wrote to her as "dearest friend and sister" and called her "mother and sweet lady".
Kylie writes that of Boniface's older friends, Bugga alone outlived the rest.
Bregwin, archbishop of Canterbury, wrote to Lul at Mainz that they kept the burial day of an abbess Bugga, whose father in Christ was Boniface.

uncertain: Her life is known from a few letters, her own and others', in Kylie's English. No source used here names her monastery or gives her years.

Whether she was also Eadburga. The Bollandists, editors of the Acta Sanctorum, report a belief that the Eadburga to whom Boniface wrote of a vision was surnamed Bugga. They place her in Kent and do not name Thanet. Kylie keeps the two women apart.
Whether Bregwin's Bugga is she. Bregwin names an abbess Bugga whose father in Christ was Boniface. The Bollandists give the same day, 27 December, for the death of their Eadburga called Bugga.
Whether Ethelbert's Abbess Bugga is the same woman. Kylie's index and introduction join them; Ethelbert names no mother and no earlier letters.

A Bugga who built a church. The index to Migne's Alcuin asks whether a Bugga who built a church, a West Saxon king's daughter, is the Bugga who wrote to Boniface. The same volume says the poem about her is not Alcuin's, since it was written under Ine, king of the West Saxons.
Kylie's dates. He dates Boniface's letter of advice to her to "About 725 (?)", with a question mark.
Her journey. Ethelbert says she met Boniface in Rome. No source used here gives the year.
